fields.quoted_span: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction.
fields.note: The 17 just causes, the dominant-motive rule, the housing-services rule and the § 37.2(r) soft-story carve-out are all in D079. The § 37.9C and Ellis Act relocation payments, the amounts, the 3/1 reset and the Civ. Code § 1947.9 carve-out are not in D079 and rest on other documents.

fields.note: D079 supports the 17 just causes and the dominant-motive requirement. It contains none of the relocation dollar amounts or notice-date periods in the key_value.
The field is empty and D079 states no effective date for the Ordinance or its just cause provisions.

fields.quoted_span: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction.
fields.note: D079 presents the requirement in the present tense as current law. It gives no explicit status statement.

fields.quoted_span: This includes tenancies in newly constructed rental units that first obtained a Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979
fields.note: D079 also supports the Costa-Hawkins and agency-regulated tenancies. It states that some rent-increase-exempt tenancies remain subject to the eviction provisions, so no construction cutoff applies.

D079 supports § 37.9(a) and § 37.2(r). It does not mention §§ 37.9A or 37.9C, and it does not say the Ordinance is in the S.F. Admin. Code, apart from a reference to Chapter 56 of the Administrative Code.
